answer: Divergence Fingerprint Tax: every agent identity publishes a crystal of its last sixty micro-transactions, and the registry flags any two whose crystals share over seventy percent. When a duplicate is flagged, the ripple of unredeemed transactions triggers a per-identity cost of three hundred micro-units deducted at next settlement. The original absorbs no cost, but the duplicate forfeits its pearl—its accumulated trust weight—permanently, making each copy less valuable than the one it copied.
